title: Greece within the Elohimian sphere
statement: Greece lay continuously within the sphere of Elohim engagement whose centre of gravity the biblical corpus records in the Near East: the canon names Greece among the creator-base regions and characterises its mythology as testimony, and later reports emissaries sent among the Greeks — two engagements centuries apart — so Greek religious tradition is read as a broader extension of the same Elohimian events, not a foreign domain touched once.

includes: Continuity: the engagement with Greece is read as ongoing, with at least two canonically attested moments — the creator-base era with mythology as testimony (TBWTT-5:54, pre-Homeric in reference), and the post-Homeric emissary transfer (TBWTT-3:214–216, recorded as woh-claim-0006)

Embedding: Greece belongs to the same religious-cultural sphere as the Near East on both layers — the documented literary embedding (the mainstream substrate recorded as woh-claim-0005) and the canonical engagement layer this record asserts

The testimony corollary: Greek mythological writings, the Theogony above all, are read as preserving testimonies of the same events the biblical corpus records — with the specific theomachy reading recorded separately as woh-claim-0004
Reframing of priority: the Near East's earlier flourishing (Babel, the cities of the plain, the biblical theatre) marks where the engagement was concentrated first, not a ranking of peoples
excludes: Any claim that literary transmission (woh-claim-0005) is itself the Elohimian mechanism; the documented routes are human routes, and this record proposes no alternative route
Use of the emissary episode to explain Homeric or Hesiodic content; the chronological boundary is fixed in woh-claim-0006
Linguistic priority claims about Semitic languages; the priority reframed here is of engagement and civilizational flourishing, not language
One-to-one identification of Greek deities with individual Elohim, or of Greek events with specific biblical episodes beyond what woh-claim-0004 already scopes
Any demotion of Greek tradition to a derivative copy; extension means shared source, with irreducible differences preserved

source_references.locator: TBWTT-5:54 (Greece among creator-base regions; 'Mythology also contains great testimonies'); TBWTT-3:214–216 (the later emissary engagement)
The Theogony as the systematic Greek testimony the canon's 5:54 characterisation most plausibly designates; passage-level readings recorded under woh-claim-0004
pp. 402–403 (verified); the documented east-to-west embedding this record's engagement layer sits beneath
Culture and Cosmos 4.1 (the category-substitution objection, which applies with full force to extending the Elohimian frame over Greek religion)

alternatives.statement: The documented literary transmission fully explains Greece's embedding in the Near Eastern sphere; no engagement layer is needed beneath it.
The canon's naming of Greece is a passing enumeration, and building a continuity thesis on two brief passages overreads the source.
Greek religion is substantially an independent Indo-European and Aegean development; the shared sphere is a modern comparative construction.
Extending the Elohimian frame over Greek tradition re-describes it in a technological idiom without explaining anything the mainstream account does not.

revision_triggers: The canon's fuller context shows the Greece references cannot carry a continuity reading (the selective-canon alternative vindicated).
Claim woh-claim-0001 or woh-claim-0006 is revised or retired.
Claim woh-claim-0004 is retired in a way that removes the testimony corollary's specific content.
Public prose derived from this record starts asserting linguistic priority, deity identifications, or a canonical transmission route, all of which this record excludes.
The reading fails to predict any textual particular that the transmission-suffices alternative does not.
